Implement the existing ping-pong HTTP API in Rust, using only a dedicated rust/ directory (do not edit files outside rust/). Match the TypeScript contract exactly: GET /ping -> 200 JSON {"message":"pong"} with application/json content type; non-GET /ping -> 405 JSON {"error":"Method Not Allowed"} plus Allow: GET; unknown routes -> 404 JSON {"error":"Not Found"}. Prefer a small idiomatic dependency-light implementation, with Cargo metadata and focused tests if appropriate. Make the changes directly in your workspace. Do not modify or delete existing files. In your final response, list every changed path and the commands/tests you ran.

I’ll inspect the existing TypeScript contract and workspace layout, then delegate a quick Rust design/test review to subagents before creating only `rust/` files. I’ll preserve every existing file and verify the implementation with focused tests.

No callable subagent tool is exposed in this workspace, so I’ll use parallel independent checks (contract discovery and repository/toolchain inspection) and reconcile their results before editing. I’ll keep the scope strictly inside `rust/`.

The contract is straightforward and dependency-free: the Rust version will use `std::net::TcpListener` with one connection per thread, emit the same JSON bodies and `application/json; charset=utf-8`, and close each response after handling it. I’m adding a small library boundary so the routing/serialization can be tested without external crates.
